items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: I got married in Chicago to a lady called Louella Brown.

ctx.x: So I went back to New York and started t' workin' in the night-clubs around in New York, 'cause ever'body know me there. Wasn't no trouble to get a gig. So I worked on Fifty-Second Street. I used to go down there to see Count Basie workin' in a little, small joint. So I got up an' sang a couple o' songs wit' him. So the man give me a job. An' they had Jimmy Rushing, me, Count Basie's band. So, I work around there for four...five years, an' then I took off and come back to California. I took off and run back to…

So I had to come out here, see about my place o' business. So I had my sister runnin' it for me. 'Course, in the meantime, I went to Chicago. I lived seventeen years in Chicago. I got married in Chicago to a lady called Louella Brown. So we got together...Cut it off [the tape recorder].
So I left back East and come to Chicago. I ran into Little Bo's (?) band again. I run into Sheila Guys again. They was workin' in a nightclub there.
